messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated CUDA_ILLEGAL_ACCESS rate detected for cluster=prod-gpu, pool=prod-gpu-nodes starting 2729876543. Error spike correlated with eviction events and OOMs. Paging-related kernel traces attached. Paging/eviction spike threshold passed. Paging/eviction-runbook notified. Pager -> @alice (oncall), @ben (sre)

alice (oncall): I'm on it. I'm seeing container restarts on node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-21. Logs show repeated 'illegal memory access' and 'misaligned device address' traces. Impacting ~10% of requests for a small subset of pods.

ben (sre): Acknowledged. Starting triage. cordoning node-gpu-17 to stop new pods: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-17` then `kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` to move workloads. Will also set scheduler preemption off for the pool as a temporary mitigation.

carla (runtime): Quick note: runtime telemetry shows KV-cache eviction concurrent with pagefault handling. Stack from dmesg on node-gpu-17: ```
[ 123456.789012] NVRM: Xid 31 detected at 0x7fefc000
[ 123456.789045] BUG: misaligned address 0x7fefc0fa in pagewalk
#0 0xffffffffffffffff do_page_fault+0x1a7
#1 0xffffffffffffffff handle_mm_fault+0x3b2
#2 0xffffffffffffffff nvidia_pagetable_walk+0x1c4
```
We see a kernel walker hitting a misaligned pointer while the runtime's pinned buffer is being evicted. Repro on canary when we force eviction + heavy KV cache hits.

dave (eng-ml): Are we on the new NVIDIA driver? We rolled drivers last week for the latest performance improvements.

carla (runtime): Yes, nodes are running nvidia-driver=535.54 (installed via daemonset). Suspect regression in driver kernel module interacting with our pinned GPU buffers during page reclamation.

emily (support): Customer impact: support telemetry shows region-us-west saw ~12 user requests fail with 500 between 14:23-14:32. I flagged the impacted tenants and started outreach. Updating status page: partial degradation.

k8s-deploy-bot: Applied temporary taint to pool prod-gpu-nodes to reduce scheduling pressure: `kubectl taint nodes -l pool=prod-gpu-nodes eviction-hotfix=true:NoSchedule`

alice (oncall): Handoff: ben will own the live mitigation (node cordon/driver rollback), carla will own runtime root cause and repro, I'll own customer comms. Logging incident in tracker INC-2026-0315-01.

ben (sre): Mitigation plan executed: rollback driver on node-gpu-17 to 525.89 via daemonset image tag `nvidia-driver:525.89-rollback`; restarted kube daemonset pods on node-gpu-17 and node-gpu-21. Commands run: ```bash
kubectl set image ds/nvidia-driver nvidia-driver=nvidia-driver:525.89-rollback -n kube-system
kubectl rollout status ds/nvidia-driver -n kube-system
```
Monitoring error rate now.

carla (runtime): Collected additional artifacts: full dmesg, gpu watchdog logs, and a core dump of the runtime process. Initial hypothesis: a race where eviction clears a GPU mapping while pagewalk in the kernel still references it -> misaligned device address in kernel. Need kernel-level repro + vendor verification.

ben (sre): Post-rollback metrics: CUDA_ILLEGAL_ACCESS events dropped from spike to baseline within 3 minutes on node-gpu-17. Rolling rollback to the remaining affected nodes (3 nodes) as a precaution. Watching 30m.

alice (oncall): Customers notified that we rolled a mitigation (driver rollback) and are monitoring. ETA for full resolution: dependent on vendor kernel patch; interim mitigations applied.

dave (eng-ml): Action items for follow-up: 1) Add driver-version dimension to alert so we can quickly filter future spikes by driver. 2) Add canary gate that runs eviction/long-running pagewalk stress test before driver rollout. 3) Evaluate runtime changes to avoid dereferencing freed pinned buffers during eviction.

emily (support): I'll compile impacted tenant list and send individualized notes. Also updating the incident channel with the customer facing blurb for review.

carla (runtime): For RCA: reproducer attached in private runbook. Will open a support case with vendor (NVIDIA) with kernel traces and repro steps. Also scheduling a deep-dive tomorrow with kernel and runtime owners.

alice (oncall): Status: MITIGATED (error rate back to normal after rollback and tainting). Not resolved. Reassign to carla for RCA and to ben for rolling remediation and playbook updates. Closing handoff in this channel.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident INC-2026-0315-01 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Notify: #postmortems, #eng-runtime.``
